questions.stem: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 17 has exactly two factors: 1 and 17. 15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7, and 9 = 3 × 3, so they are all composite.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorization of 30?
questions.explanation: 30 = 2 × 15 = 2 × 3 × 5. All three factors (2, 3, 5) are prime, so 2 × 3 × 5 is the prime factorization.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorization of 18?
questions.explanation: 18 = 2 × 9 = 2 × 3 × 3. Both 2 and 3 are prime, so 2 × 3 × 3 is the prime factorization.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is composite?
questions.explanation: 27 = 3 × 9 = 3 × 3 × 3, so it has more than two factors. 23, 29, and 31 are all prime.

questions.stem: Two students found different factor trees for 60. Student A started with 2 × 30. Student B started with 6 × 10. Which statement is true?
choices: Both get the same prime factorization: 2 × 2 × 3 × 5
Only Student A gets the correct prime factorization
Only Student B gets the correct prime factorization
They will get different prime factorizations
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic says every composite number has exactly one prime factorization. No matter how you start the factor tree, you always end with 2 × 2 × 3 × 5.

questions.stem: The first lock panel shows 90. What is the prime factorization of 90?
questions.explanation: 90 = 2 × 45 = 2 × 9 × 5 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 5. Every factor is prime, so the lock accepts 2 × 3 × 3 × 5.

questions.stem: The second panel needs a number whose prime factorization is 2² × 3². Which number unlocks it?
questions.explanation: 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36, so 36 is the code for this panel.

questions.stem: The final lock asks for the prime factorization of 78 written as a product of primes. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: 78 = 2 × 39 = 2 × 3 × 13. All three factors are prime, so 2 × 3 × 13 unlocks the final panel.

questions.explanation: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. A composite number has more than two factors.

questions.stem: What is the GCF of 8 and 12?
questions.explanation: Factors of 8: 1, 2, 4, 8. Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The largest common factor is 4.

questions.stem: Which pair of numbers has a GCF of 5?
questions.explanation: 15 = 3 × 5, 25 = 5 × 5. Both share the factor 5, and 5 is the largest shared factor.

questions.stem: What is the GCF of 14 and 21?
questions.explanation: Factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14. Factors of 21: 1, 3, 7, 21. The largest common factor is 7.

questions.stem: What is the GCF of 9 and 15?
questions.explanation: Factors of 9: 1, 3, 9. Factors of 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. The largest common factor is 3.

questions.stem: A teacher has 36 pencils and 48 erasers. She wants to make identical supply bags with no items left over. What is the greatest number of bags she can make?
questions.explanation: GCF(36, 48) = 12. She can make 12 bags, each with 3 pencils and 4 erasers.

questions.stem: Mission Control must split 24 oxygen tanks and 36 ration packs into identical crew pods with none left over. What is the GCF of 24 and 36?
questions.explanation: Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The greatest shared factor is 12, so 12 pods can be filled equally.

questions.stem: The astronaut crew has 40 solar cells and 60 battery cells to load into matching storage bins with nothing left over. What is the GCF of 40 and 60?
questions.explanation: Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Factors of 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60. The greatest shared factor is 20, so 20 bins can be filled equally.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Factor"?
questions.explanation: 3 for the number 12: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 with no remainder.

questions.stem: Which statement about "Greatest Common Factor" is true?
choices: The greatest common factor of 12 and 18 is 2.
The greatest common factor of 12 and 18 is 6.
The greatest common factor of 12 and 18 is 36.
questions.explanation: Correct: The greatest common factor of 12 and 18 is 6.

questions.stem: What is the LCM of 3 and 5?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, ... Multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, ... The smallest common multiple is 15.

questions.stem: What is the LCM of 6 and 8?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, ... Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, ... The smallest common multiple is 24.

questions.stem: What is the LCM of 4 and 10?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, ... Multiples of 10: 10, 20, ... The smallest common multiple is 20.

questions.stem: What is the LCM of 2 and 7?
questions.explanation: Since 2 and 7 share no common factors (they are relatively prime), LCM = 2 × 7 = 14.

questions.stem: Two buses leave the station at 8:00 AM. Bus A returns every 15 minutes and Bus B returns every 20 minutes. When is the next time both buses are at the station together?
questions.explanation: LCM(15, 20) = 60 minutes. Both buses return together 60 minutes after 8:00 AM, at 9:00 AM.

questions.stem: Stop 1 — Oxygen Bay: The oxygen scrubber cycles every 4 minutes and the air filter cycles every 6 minutes. They both just ran together. After how many minutes do they next run together?
questions.explanation: Skip count: multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12; multiples of 6 are 6, 12. The first shared multiple is LCM(4, 6) = 12 minutes.

questions.stem: Stop 2 — Docking Ring: A supply pod arrives every 8 minutes and a cargo shuttle arrives every 12 minutes. They just docked together. After how many minutes do they next dock together?
questions.explanation: LCM(8, 12) = 24. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24; multiples of 12: 12, 24. The first shared multiple is 24 minutes.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Multiple"?
questions.explanation: 12 is a multiple of 4: 4 × 3 = 12.

questions.stem: Which statement about "Least common multiple" is true?
choices: The least common multiple of 4 and 6 is 24.
The least common multiple of 4 and 6 is 2.
The least common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12.
questions.explanation: Correct: The least common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12.

questions.explanation: Line up decimals: 9.05 + 4.70. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 0 + 7 = 7. Ones: 9 + 4 = 13. Answer: 13.75.

questions.stem: What is 50 − 23.47?
questions.explanation: Rewrite 50 as 50.00. Then 50.00 − 23.47 = 26.53. You must borrow across multiple places.

questions.stem: A student buys items costing $4.59, $12.75, and $3.80. What is the total cost?
questions.explanation: 4.59 + 12.75 + 3.80 = 21.14. Line up decimal points and add column by column.

questions.stem: Case File: A crew member's snack receipt shows $27.60 for dried fruit and $15.45 for protein bars. What is the total on the receipt?
questions.explanation: Line up the decimal points: 27.60 + 15.45. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 6 + 4 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Ones: 7 + 5 + 1 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Tens: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Total: $43.05.

questions.stem: Case File: The oxygen gauge dropped from 9.6 units to a new reading after the crew used 4.75 units. How much oxygen is left?
questions.explanation: Annex a zero so 9.6 becomes 9.60, then subtract: 9.60 − 4.75 = 4.85 units. Borrow in the hundredths and tenths places to subtract correctly.

questions.stem: Case File: A supply log started the shift with $48.00 in the station snack fund. By the end, $31.27 had been spent. How much is left in the fund?
questions.explanation: Write 48.00 − 31.27 with points lined up. Hundredths: 0 − 7 → borrow → 10 − 7 = 3. Tenths: 9 − 2 = 7 (after borrowing). Ones: 7 − 1 = 6. Tens: 4 − 3 = 1. Answer: $16.73.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Tenths"?

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Hundredths"?

questions.stem: Which estimate is closest to 4.8 × 3.2?

questions.stem: A car travels 55.5 miles per hour for 2.4 hours. How far does it go?
questions.explanation: 555 × 24 = 13,320. Total decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 133.20 = 133.2 miles.

questions.stem: A customer orders 3 taco baskets at $4.25 each. What is the total before tax?
questions.explanation: 3 × 425 = 1,275. The factor $4.25 has 2 decimal places, so 3 × $4.25 = $12.75.

questions.stem: The truck sells 2.5 pounds of fries, and each pound earns $1.20 in profit. What is the total profit? (2.5 × 1.2)

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Decimal places"?

questions.stem: Table 1 splits a $15.00 lunch bill equally among 4 friends. How much does each friend pay?
questions.explanation: $15.00 ÷ 4 = $3.75. Each friend pays $3.75.

questions.stem: A recipe uses 9.6 cups of flour to make 3 equal batches of muffins. How many cups of flour go in each batch?
questions.explanation: 9.6 ÷ 3 = 3.2 cups in each batch.

questions.stem: The arcade corner has 4.8 meters of token ribbon, cut into 0.6-meter prize strips. How many strips can the cafe make?
questions.explanation: Multiply both by 10: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 strips.

questions.explanation: Volume measures 3D space, so it uses cubic units like in³. Square units (in²) are for area, and inches are for length.

questions.stem: Two storage bins: Bin A is 8 × 6 × 5 inches. Bin B is 9 × 4 × 7 inches. Which holds more and by how much?
questions.explanation: Bin A: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Bin B: 9 × 4 × 7 = 252 in³. Bin B holds 12 in³ more.

questions.explanation: Prism A volume = 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cm³. For Prism B, h = 48 ÷ (8 × 3) = 48 ÷ 24 = 2 cm.

questions.stem: A time capsule box is 5 units long, 3 units wide, and 2 units tall. How many unit cubes fill it?

questions.stem: You stack unit cubes in a capsule: each layer has 6 cubes, and there are 4 layers. What is the volume?
questions.explanation: Each layer has 6 cubes and there are 4 layers, so 6 × 4 = 24 cubic units. This is the same as length × width × height with one factor being the number of layers.

questions.stem: Two boxes: Box A is 10 × 5 × 4 inches. Box B is 8 × 6 × 5 inches. Which has more volume and by how much?
questions.explanation: Box A: 10 × 5 × 4 = 200 in³. Box B: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Box B is bigger by 40 in³.

questions.stem: What is the volume of a prism with edge lengths 1/2 m, 3 m, and 4 m?
A cube has an edge length of 5 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: A cube's volume is edge³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cm³.

questions.stem: A fish tank measures 2 1/2 ft by 2 ft by 3 ft. What is its volume?
A prism with a 3/4 ft by 2 ft base has a volume of 9 ft³. What is its height?
questions.explanation: Height = V ÷ (base area) = 9 ÷ (3/4 × 2) = 9 ÷ 1.5 = 6 ft.

questions.stem: A time-capsule box measures 6 in long, 4 in wide, and 3 in tall. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: V = length × width × height = 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 cubic in. Volume uses cubic units.

questions.stem: Two storage boxes are ready to pack. Box A is 5 × 5 × 2 inches and Box B is 4 × 4 × 3 inches. Which box holds more?
choices: Box A, because 50 cubic in is more than 48 cubic in
Box B, because 48 cubic in is more than 50 cubic in
Box B, because it is taller
questions.explanation: Box A: 5 × 5 × 2 = 50 cubic in. Box B: 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cubic in. 50 > 48, so Box A holds more.

questions.stem: A keepsake box is 4 in long, 3 in wide, and 1½ in tall. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: V = 4 × 3 × 1.5 = 12 × 1.5 = 18 cubic in. A fractional edge does not change the steps.

questions.stem: A rectangular prism has l = 6 in, w = 4 in, h = 2 in. What is its surface area?
How many faces does a rectangular prism have?
questions.explanation: A rectangular prism has 6 faces: top, bottom, front, back, left, and right.

questions.stem: Surface area is measured in which type of unit?
questions.explanation: Surface area measures flat surfaces, so it uses square units. Volume uses cubic units.

questions.stem: A cube has edges of 5 cm. What is its surface area?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 identical faces. Each face: 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Total SA = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².

questions.stem: You unfold a time capsule that is a cube. Its net shows 6 equal squares, and each square has an area of 4 cm². What is the cube's total surface area?
questions.explanation: A cube net has 6 equal square faces. With each face 4 cm², the surface area is 6 × 4 = 24 cm².

questions.stem: Your team unfolds a rectangular time capsule box into a flat net. How many faces (flat sides) will the net show in all?
questions.explanation: A rectangular prism has 6 faces — top, bottom, front, back, left, and right — so its net shows 6 faces.

Which one is an example of "Net"?
choices: Six connected rectangles that fold into a box
questions.explanation: Six connected rectangles that fold into a box: It folds up into a solid.

questions.stem: What is the surface area of a rectangular prism with l = 5 cm, w = 4 cm, h = 3 cm?
How many faces does a triangular prism have?
questions.explanation: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangular bases and 3 rectangular lateral faces.

questions.stem: A triangular prism has two triangular bases each with area 12 cm² and three rectangular faces with areas 30 cm², 40 cm², and 40 cm². What is the total surface area?
A triangular prism has triangular bases with base 6 in and height 4 in. The prism is 10 in long and the two slant sides of the triangle are each 5 in. What is the surface area?
questions.explanation: Triangular bases: 2 × (½ × 6 × 4) = 24 in². Three rectangular faces: 6(10) + 5(10) + 5(10) = 60 + 50 + 50 = 160 in². SA = 24 + 160 = 184 in².

questions.stem: A rectangular time capsule box measures 3 in by 4 in by 5 in. How much wrapping paper covers its surface (no overlap)?

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Triangular prism"?
choices: A tent shape with triangle ends
questions.explanation: A tent shape with triangle ends: It has two triangular faces and three rectangular faces.

questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base edge of 5 in and a slant height of 7 in. What is the surface area?
questions.explanation: Base: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Each lateral face: ½ × 5 × 7 = 17.5 in². Four faces: 4 × 17.5 = 70 in². SA = 25 + 70 = 95 in².

questions.stem: How many lateral (triangular) faces does a square pyramid have?
questions.explanation: A square pyramid has a square base and 4 triangular lateral faces — one for each side of the square.

questions.stem: What is the area of one triangular face with base 8 in and slant height 6 in?
questions.explanation: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 in².

questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base area of 49 cm² and a total lateral area of 84 cm². What is the surface area?
questions.explanation: SA = Base Area + Lateral Area = 49 + 84 = 133 cm².

questions.stem: Your first gift box is a square pyramid with a base edge of 7 in and a slant height of 9 in. How much wrapping paper (total surface area) covers it?
questions.explanation: Base: 7 × 7 = 49 in². One triangular face: ½ × 7 × 9 = 31.5 in². Four faces: 4 × 31.5 = 126 in². SA = 49 + 126 = 175 in². Surface area uses square units (in²).

questions.stem: Before adding the base, you need the area of just one triangular face of a gift box with base edge 8 in and slant height 5 in. What is it?
questions.explanation: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 in². You use the slant height (5) as the triangle's height, not the pyramid's vertical height.

questions.stem: A gift box is a square pyramid with a base edge of 9 in. What is the area of its square base (the part that sits on the table)?
questions.explanation: The base is a square, so base area = side × side = 9 × 9 = 81 in². You would still add the four triangular faces to get the full surface area.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Pyramid"?
choices: A box with six rectangular faces
A square base with four triangle sides meeting at a top point
questions.explanation: A square base with four triangle sides meeting at a top point: Its triangular faces meet at one apex.

questions.stem: What does 3 ÷ 1/4 mean?
questions.explanation: 3 ÷ 1/4 asks: how many 1/4-size pieces fit into 3? The answer is 12, because each whole has 4 fourths, and 3 × 4 = 12.

questions.stem: Which expression means 'how many 1/3-size pieces are in 2'?
questions.explanation: Finding how many 1/3-size pieces fit into 2 is represented by 2 ÷ 1/3. The answer is 6.

questions.stem: A rope is 4 feet long. How many 1/2-foot pieces can be cut from it?
questions.explanation: 4 ÷ 1/2 = 4 × 2 = 8 pieces. Each whole foot contains 2 halves, and 4 × 2 = 8.

questions.stem: What is 6 ÷ 1/5?
questions.explanation: 6 ÷ 1/5 means how many 1/5-size pieces fit into 6. Each whole has 5 fifths, so 6 × 5 = 30.

questions.stem: A shelf is 5 feet long. Books are each 1/4 foot wide. How many books fit on the shelf? Which expression represents this?
questions.explanation: You are finding how many 1/4-foot pieces fit into 5 feet, which is 5 ÷ 1/4 = 5 × 4 = 20 books.

questions.stem: Agent Cole has 8 feet of evidence rope and cuts it into 1/3-foot pieces for tagging. What does 8 ÷ 1/3 mean?
choices: How many 1/3-foot pieces fit into 8 feet
8 feet shortened by 1/3 of a foot
8 pieces that are each 1/3 foot long
questions.explanation: Dividing by 1/3 asks how many 1/3-foot pieces fit into 8 feet. Each foot holds 3 thirds, so 8 × 3 = 24 pieces.

questions.stem: Picture clue: a 5-inch fingerprint strip is split into 1/6-inch slivers under the microscope. Which division does the picture show, and what is the count?
questions.explanation: How many 1/6-inch slivers fit into 5 inches? Each inch holds 6 sixths, so 5 × 6 = 30 slivers.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Reciprocal"?
questions.explanation: The reciprocal of 3/4 is 4/3: Flipping 3/4 gives 4/3.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Unit fraction"?
questions.explanation: 1/8: Its numerator is 1.

questions.stem: What does 3 ÷ 1/4 mean?
questions.explanation: 3 ÷ 1/4 asks: how many 1/4-size pieces fit into 3? The answer is 12, because each whole has 4 fourths, and 3 × 4 = 12.

questions.stem: Which expression means 'how many 1/3-size pieces are in 2'?
questions.explanation: Finding how many 1/3-size pieces fit into 2 is represented by 2 ÷ 1/3. The answer is 6.

questions.stem: A rope is 4 feet long. How many 1/2-foot pieces can be cut from it?
questions.explanation: 4 ÷ 1/2 = 4 × 2 = 8 pieces. Each whole foot contains 2 halves, and 4 × 2 = 8.

questions.stem: What is 6 ÷ 1/5?
questions.explanation: 6 ÷ 1/5 means how many 1/5-size pieces fit into 6. Each whole has 5 fifths, so 6 × 5 = 30.

questions.stem: A shelf is 5 feet long. Books are each 1/4 foot wide. How many books fit on the shelf? Which expression represents this?
questions.explanation: You are finding how many 1/4-foot pieces fit into 5 feet, which is 5 ÷ 1/4 = 5 × 4 = 20 books.

questions.stem: Clue 1 — The case file says a 3-cup bottle of fingerprint dust must be poured into evidence vials that each hold 1/4 cup. Which question does 3 ÷ 1/4 ask?
choices: How many 1/4-cup vials fit into 3 cups
How many 3-cup bottles fit into 1/4 cup
questions.explanation: Dividing by a fraction asks how many of that piece fit inside the whole. 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12, so the dust fills 12 vials.

questions.stem: Clue 2 — A roll of evidence tape is 8 feet long. The lab marks it into 1/4-foot sections. How many sections are made, and which expression proves it?
questions.explanation: Each foot holds 4 fourths, so 8 feet hold 8 × 4 = 32 sections. The matching expression is 8 ÷ 1/4 = 32.

questions.stem: Clue 5 — Detective Reyes pours 5 quarts of evidence solution into beakers that each hold 1/3 quart. She wants to know how many beakers she fills. What does the quotient of 5 ÷ 1/3 tell her in this story?
choices: The number of 1/3-quart beakers she can fill, which is 15
The number of quarts in one beaker, which is 1/3
How much solution is left over, which is 5
How many quarts each beaker loses, which is 3
questions.explanation: 5 ÷ 1/3 asks how many 1/3-quart beakers fit into 5 quarts. Each quart holds 3 thirds, so 5 × 3 = 15 beakers.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Reciprocal"?
questions.explanation: The reciprocal of 3/4 is 4/3: Flipping 3/4 gives 4/3.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Unit fraction"?
questions.explanation: 1/8: Its numerator is 1.

questions.stem: What is 6 ÷ 1/3?
questions.explanation: 6 ÷ 1/3 = 6 × 3/1 = 18. There are 18 thirds in 6 wholes.

questions.stem: What is 3 ÷ 1/5?
questions.explanation: 3 ÷ 1/5 = 3 × 5/1 = 15. There are 15 fifths in 3 wholes.

questions.stem: What is 10 ÷ 1/4?
questions.explanation: 10 ÷ 1/4 = 10 × 4/1 = 40. There are 40 quarter-size pieces in 10 wholes.

questions.stem: What is 5 ÷ 1/2?
questions.explanation: 5 ÷ 1/2 = 5 × 2/1 = 10. There are 10 halves in 5 wholes.

questions.stem: What is 6 ÷ 2/3?
Detective Park has 4 cups of flour. Each batch of evidence-cookies needs 1/2 cup. How many batches can he make?
questions.explanation: 4 ÷ 1/2 = 4 × 2/1 = 8 batches. Each cup makes 2 half-cup batches.

questions.stem: The crew has 8 quarts of sports drink. Each detective's water bottle holds 4/5 of a quart. How many bottles can be filled?
There are 3 bags of trail mix. Each snack pouch needs 2/3 of a bag. How many full pouches can be filled, and is there a leftover?
choices: 4 1/2 pouches (4 full, half a pouch left)
questions.explanation: 3 ÷ 2/3 = 3 × 3/2 = 9/2 = 4 1/2. You can fill 4 full pouches with half a pouch of mix left over.

questions.stem: Detective Park bakes with 9 cups of batter. Each muffin pan holds 3/4 of a cup. How many pans can he fill?
What is the reciprocal of 3/5?
questions.explanation: To find the reciprocal, flip the fraction. The reciprocal of 3/5 is 5/3.

questions.stem: What is 1/2 ÷ 1/4?
questions.explanation: 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2. Two 1/4-size pieces fit into 1/2.

questions.stem: What is 3/4 ÷ 1/8?
What is 2/3 ÷ 1/3?
questions.explanation: 2/3 ÷ 1/3 = 2/3 × 3/1 = 6/3 = 2. Two 1/3-size pieces fit into 2/3.

questions.stem: A recipe needs 2/3 cup of sugar. You only have a 1/6-cup scoop. How many scoops do you need?
Lock 1 — Crack the code: What is (1/2) ÷ (1/4) in simplest form?
questions.explanation: (1/2) ÷ (1/4) = (1/2) × (4/1) = 4/2 = 2. Two 1/4-size pieces fit into 1/2, so the lock opens on 2.

questions.stem: Lock 2 — The vault dial reads a fraction problem: What is (2/3) ÷ (1/6) in simplest form?
Lock 3 — Decode the keypad: What is (3/4) ÷ (1/2) in simplest form?
What is 1 1/2 ÷ 3/4?
Convert 3 2/5 to an improper fraction.
What is 2 1/4 ÷ 3/4?
What is 3 1/2 ÷ 1/4?
A recipe makes 2 1/4 batches of cookies. Each batch uses 3/4 cup of butter. How many cups of butter are needed in total?
questions.explanation: This is multiplication: 2 1/4 × 3/4 = 9/4 × 3/4 = 27/16. Wait — re-read: we need 2 1/4 batches at 3/4 cup each, but the question for division practice should be: if you have 2 1/4 cups and each batch needs 3/4 cup, how many batches? 2 1/4 ÷ 3/4 = 9/4 × 4/3 = 36/12 = 3.

questions.stem: Mission 1: The stakeout shift is 4 1/2 hours long. Each agent covers a 1 1/2-hour watch. How many agent watches fill one shift?
Mission 2: A surveillance route is 3 miles long, split into 1 1/2-mile patrol sections. How many sections are on the route?
Mission 3: There are 7 1/2 feet of caution tape to seal a crime scene. Each doorway needs 2 1/2 feet. How many doorways can be sealed?
Which one is an example of "Mixed Number"?
questions.explanation: 2 1/3: It has a whole part (2) and a fraction part (1/3).

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Improper Fraction"?
questions.explanation: 7/3: The numerator 7 is greater than the denominator 3.

questions.stem: A ribbon is 4/5 of a yard long. Each bow uses 1/10 of a yard. Which equation finds how many bows can be made?
questions.explanation: The total (4/5 yard) is divided into groups of 1/10 yard each. The equation is 4/5 ÷ 1/10 = 4/5 × 10/1 = 40/5 = 8 bows.

questions.stem: A detective has 1/2 gallon of solution. Each test uses 1/8 gallon. How many tests can be run?
A trail is 3/4 mile long. A jogger runs laps of 1/4 mile each. How many laps does the jogger complete?
questions.explanation: 3/4 ÷ 1/4 = 3/4 × 4/1 = 12/4 = 3 laps. This is reasonable: three 1/4-mile pieces fit into 3/4 mile.

questions.stem: A board is 5/6 foot long. Each shelf bracket needs 1/6 foot. How many brackets fit?
Marcus solved 2/3 ÷ 1/4 and got 8/3 = 2 2/3. He says 'That can't be right because I started with less than 1.' Is Marcus's math correct? Is his reasoning correct?
choices: His math is correct (2 2/3), but his reasoning is wrong — dividing by a small fraction gives a larger result
His math and reasoning are both correct — the answer should be less than 1
His math is wrong — the answer should be 1/6
His math is wrong — the answer should be 8/12
questions.explanation: 2/3 ÷ 1/4 = 2/3 × 4/1 = 8/3 = 2 2/3. This IS correct. When you divide by a number less than 1, the quotient is greater than the dividend.

questions.stem: Room 1 — Evidence Locker: Agent Torres has 7/8 pound of casting clay to lift footprints. Each cast uses 1/8 pound. How many casts can she make to unlock the door?
questions.explanation: The total (7/8 lb) is the dividend and each cast (1/8 lb) is the divisor: 7/8 ÷ 1/8 = 7/8 × 8/1 = 56/8 = 7 casts.

questions.stem: Room 2 — Surveillance Map: A suspect's trail is 5/6 of a mile. Hidden checkpoints are spaced every 1/6 of a mile. How many checkpoints are on the trail?
questions.explanation: The total distance (5/6 mile) is the dividend and the checkpoint spacing (1/6 mile) is the divisor: 5/6 ÷ 1/6 = 5/6 × 6/1 = 30/6 = 5 checkpoints.

questions.stem: Room 5 — Final Keypad: The vault key code equals the number of 3/10-liter vials Torres can fill from a 9/10-liter bottle of fingerprint solution. What is the code?
questions.explanation: The total (9/10 liter) is the dividend and each vial (3/10 liter) is the divisor: 9/10 ÷ 3/10 = 9/10 × 10/3 = 90/30 = 3 vials, so the code is 3.

questions.stem: A recipe uses 4 cups of milk and 1 cup of cream. What is the ratio of milk to cream?
questions.explanation: A ratio compares quantities in the order given. Milk to cream = 4 to 1, or 4:1.

questions.stem: Chef Reyes uses 6 strawberries and 2 bananas in a smoothie. What is the part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit?
questions.explanation: Total fruit = 6 + 2 = 8. The part-to-whole ratio of bananas to total fruit is 2:8.

questions.stem: In a class of 30 students, 18 are girls. What is the part-to-part ratio of boys to girls?
questions.explanation: Boys = 30 − 18 = 12. Part-to-part ratio of boys to girls = 12:18. (Order matters!)

questions.stem: A pet store has 5 dogs and 9 cats. What is the ratio of dogs to cats?
questions.explanation: The ratio of dogs to cats compares dogs first, then cats: 5 to 9, or 5:9.

questions.stem: A fruit salad has 5 pieces of melon, 3 pieces of pineapple, and 2 grapes. What is the ratio of pineapple to melon?
questions.explanation: The ratio of pineapple to melon compares pineapple (3) to melon (5), so the ratio is 3:5.

questions.stem: A parking lot has 10 cars and 6 trucks. What is the part-to-whole ratio of trucks to total vehicles?
questions.explanation: Total vehicles = 10 + 6 = 16. The ratio of trucks to total is 6:16.

questions.stem: Prep Bowl A: Chef Reyes stirs 7 cups of flour with 4 cups of water to make dough. What is the part-to-part ratio of flour to water?
questions.explanation: Part-to-part compares the two ingredients in the order named. Flour to water = 7 to 4, written 7:4.

questions.stem: Kitchen Crew: A cooking class has 5 student chefs and 7 student helpers, for 12 students in all. What is the part-to-whole ratio of student chefs to the whole class?
questions.explanation: The whole class is 5 + 7 = 12 students. Part-to-whole compares one part to the total, so chefs to whole class is 5:12.

questions.stem: “For every” language: Chef Reyes says, “My glaze uses 9 spoons of honey for every 4 spoons of lemon.” Written in colon notation, the ratio of honey to lemon is:
questions.explanation: “For every 9 honey to 4 lemon” is a part-to-part comparison. In colon notation, honey to lemon is 9:4.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Part-to-part"?
questions.explanation: 2 red marbles to 3 blue marbles: It compares one part to another part.

questions.explanation: The ratio of pineapple to melon compares pineapple (3) to melon (5), so the ratio is 3:5.

questions.stem: A parking lot has 10 cars and 6 trucks. What is the part-to-whole ratio of trucks to total vehicles?
questions.explanation: Total vehicles = 10 + 6 = 16. The ratio of trucks to total is 6:16.

questions.stem: Station 1 — Sauce Bench: Chef Reyes mixes 3 cups of tomato sauce with 2 cups of cream. What is the ratio of tomato sauce to cream?
questions.explanation: A ratio compares the two amounts in the order named. Tomato sauce to cream = 3 to 2, written 3:2.

questions.stem: Station 2 — Fruit Tray: A tray holds 4 strawberries and 6 blueberries. What is the part-to-whole ratio of strawberries to total berries?
questions.explanation: Total berries = 4 + 6 = 10. The part-to-whole ratio of strawberries to total is 4:10.

questions.stem: Station 5 — Soup Pot: A soup uses 8 cups of broth and 3 cups of noodles. What is the ratio of broth to noodles?
questions.explanation: Broth is named first, then noodles, so the ratio is 8 to 3, written 8:3.

questions.stem: A recipe uses 3 eggs for every 5 cups of flour. How many eggs are needed for 15 cups of flour?
questions.explanation: The scale factor is 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Multiply the eggs by 3: 3 × 3 = 9 eggs.

questions.stem: Which row does NOT belong in a ratio table for 4:5?
questions.explanation: 6:10 simplifies to 3:5, not 4:5. The other ratios (8:10, 12:15, 16:20) all simplify to 4:5.

questions.stem: A ratio table shows 3:7, 6:14, and 9:21. What is the next row?
questions.explanation: The pattern adds 3 to the first value and 7 to the second each time. After 9:21: 9+3=12 and 21+7=28. The next row is 12:28.

questions.stem: A ratio table for 2:5 starts with 2:5, 4:10. What is the third row?
questions.explanation: The additive pattern adds 2 to the first value and 5 to the second. 4+2=6 and 10+5=15. The third row is 6:15.

questions.stem: In a ratio table, the ratio of sugar to butter is 3:2. If you use 12 cups of sugar, how many cups of butter do you need?
questions.explanation: Scale factor: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Multiply butter by 4: 2 × 4 = 8 cups of butter.

questions.stem: A ratio table shows 5:8, 10:16, 15:24. What scale factor was used from the first row to the third row?
questions.explanation: From 5 to 15: 15 ÷ 5 = 3. From 8 to 24: 24 ÷ 8 = 3. The scale factor is 3.

questions.stem: The food truck sells tacos at a steady rate: 2 tacos cost $5. At that rate, how much do 6 tacos cost?
questions.explanation: 6 tacos is 3 times 2 tacos, so multiply the cost by 3: $5 x 3 = $15.

questions.stem: A smoothie recipe at the truck uses 4 cups of mango for every 3 cups of pineapple. How many cups of mango are needed for 9 cups of pineapple?
questions.explanation: The scale factor is 9 div 3 = 3. Multiply the mango by 3: 4 x 3 = 12 cups.

questions.stem: Which statement about "Equivalent ratio" is true?
questions.explanation: Correct: 2:3 and 4:6 are equivalent ratios.

questions.stem: A ratio table shows (2, 6), (4, 12), and (6, 18). Which ordered pair comes next if the pattern continues?
questions.explanation: The pattern adds 2 to x and 6 to y each time. After (6, 18): x = 6+2 = 8, y = 18+6 = 24. The next point is (8, 24).

questions.stem: When you graph equivalent ratios, the points will always form what shape?
choices: A straight line through the origin
questions.explanation: Equivalent ratios are proportional, so their graph is always a straight line that passes through the origin (0, 0).

questions.stem: A ratio table shows (2, 8), (3, 12), and (5, 20). What is the y-value when x = 7?
questions.explanation: The ratio is y/x = 8/2 = 4. For every x, y = 4x. When x = 7: y = 4 × 7 = 28.

questions.stem: Which point would NOT be on the graph of the ratio 1:5?
questions.explanation: For the ratio 1:5, every y-value should be 5 times the x-value. (3, 10): 5 × 3 = 15, not 10. So (3, 10) does not belong.

questions.stem: Points from a ratio table are plotted at (1, 4), (2, 8), and (3, 12). What is the ratio of y to x for each point?
questions.explanation: For each point: 4÷1 = 4, 8÷2 = 4, 12÷3 = 4. The ratio of y to x is always 4:1.

questions.stem: Two students graph ratio tables. Student A plots (1,2), (2,4), (3,6). Student B plots (1,3), (2,6), (3,9). Whose line is steeper?
questions.explanation: Student A's ratio is 1:2 (y goes up 2 for each 1 in x). Student B's ratio is 1:3 (y goes up 3 for each 1 in x). A higher rate of change means a steeper line, so Student B's is steeper.

questions.stem: The smoothie recipe is 1 cup of blueberries to 2 scoops of yogurt. If cups go on the x-axis and scoops on the y-axis, which ordered pair shows 3 cups of blueberries?
questions.explanation: Cups (x) come first, scoops (y) second. 3 cups need 3 × 2 = 6 scoops, so the point is (3, 6).

questions.stem: On the smoothie graph, every point follows the rule scoops = 2 × cups. Which equation describes the pattern between x (cups) and y (scoops)?
questions.explanation: Each cup needs 2 scoops, so y (scoops) is always 2 times x (cups): y = 2x. For 4 cups, y = 2 × 4 = 8.

questions.stem: Which ratio is equivalent to 2:5?
questions.explanation: Multiply both parts by 2: 2×2 = 4 and 5×2 = 10, so 4:10 is equivalent to 2:5.

questions.stem: A recipe uses 4 eggs for every 6 cups of flour. Which ratio is equivalent?
questions.explanation: Divide both by 2: 4÷2 = 2 and 6÷2 = 3. The ratio 2:3 is equivalent to 4:6.

questions.stem: Which ratio is NOT equivalent to 6:9?
questions.explanation: 6:9 simplifies to 2:3. Check each: 2:3 ✓, 12:18 = 2:3 ✓, 18:27 = 2:3 ✓. But 3:5 does not simplify to 2:3.

questions.stem: What is the simplest form of the ratio 15:25?
questions.explanation: The GCF of 15 and 25 is 5. Divide both by 5: 15÷5 = 3 and 25÷5 = 5. The simplest form is 3:5.

questions.stem: Marcus earns $45 for every 3 hours of work. How much does he earn in 8 hours?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: $45 ÷ 3 = $15/hour. In 8 hours: $15 × 8 = $120.

questions.stem: Chef Montoya's dressing uses 3 spoons of oil to 4 spoons of vinegar (3:4). Which recipe card shows an EQUIVALENT ratio?
questions.explanation: Multiply both parts of 3:4 by 3: 3 x 3 = 9 and 4 x 3 = 12, so 9:12 is equivalent to 3:4.

questions.stem: The lemonade station mixes 5 cups of lemon juice to 2 cups of sugar (5:2). Which batch keeps the SAME taste?
questions.explanation: Multiply both parts of 5:2 by 3: 5 x 3 = 15 and 2 x 3 = 6, so 15:6 is equivalent to 5:2.

questions.stem: Which statement about "Equivalent ratios" is true?
questions.explanation: Correct: 6:9 and 2:3 are equivalent ratios.

questions.stem: Chef A uses 2 cups of cheese for every 8 crackers. Chef B uses 3 cups of cheese for every 9 crackers. Who uses more cheese per cracker?
questions.explanation: Chef A: 2÷8 = 0.25 cups per cracker. Chef B: 3÷9 ≈ 0.33 cups per cracker. Chef B uses more cheese per cracker.

questions.stem: Which ratio is greater: 3:4 or 5:8?
questions.explanation: Convert to the same denominator: 3:4 = 6:8. Since 6:8 > 5:8, the ratio 3:4 is greater.

questions.stem: Which lemonade recipe is more lemony? Recipe A: 2 lemons for 6 cups of water. Recipe B: 3 lemons for 7 cups of water.
questions.explanation: Recipe A: 2÷6 ≈ 0.33 lemons per cup. Recipe B: 3÷7 ≈ 0.43 lemons per cup. Since 0.43 > 0.33, Recipe B is more lemony.

questions.stem: Which is the better deal: 4 apples for $3 or 6 apples for $5?
questions.explanation: Deal 1: $3÷4 = $0.75 per apple. Deal 2: $5÷6 ≈ $0.83 per apple. $0.75 < $0.83, so 4 apples for $3 is the better deal.

questions.stem: Store A sells 3 mangoes for $6. Store B sells 5 mangoes for $9. Which store offers a better price per mango?
questions.explanation: Store A: $6÷3 = $2.00 per mango. Store B: $9÷5 = $1.80 per mango. Store B has the better (lower) price per mango.

questions.stem: Chef Academy's snack bar sells 3 mini quiches for $6 or 5 mini quiches for $8. Which is the better deal per quiche?
questions.explanation: 3 for $6 is $6 / 3 = $2.00 per quiche. 5 for $8 is $8 / 5 = $1.60 per quiche. $1.60 < $2.00, so 5 quiches for $8 is the better deal.

questions.stem: Two soup recipes use salt. Recipe A uses 4 tsp salt for 10 cups of broth. Recipe B uses 3 tsp salt for 8 cups of broth. Which soup is saltier per cup?
questions.explanation: Recipe A: 4 / 10 = 0.4 tsp per cup. Recipe B: 3 / 8 = 0.375 tsp per cup. Since 0.4 > 0.375, Recipe A is saltier per cup.

questions.stem: Chef Mara's lemon glaze uses 6 oz of lemon juice for 9 cupcakes. Chef Devi's uses 4 oz for 7 cupcakes. Whose glaze has more lemon per cupcake?
questions.explanation: Chef Mara: 6 / 9 = 0.666... oz per cupcake. Chef Devi: 4 / 7 = 0.571... oz per cupcake. Since 0.67 > 0.57, Chef Mara's glaze has more lemon per cupcake.

questions.stem: Which statement about "Equivalent ratio" is true?
questions.explanation: Correct: 4:5 and 8:10 are equivalent ratios.

questions.stem: A recipe uses 4 cups of broth for every 10 servings. How many cups of broth are needed for 30 servings?
questions.explanation: Scale factor: 30 ÷ 10 = 3. Multiply broth by 3: 4 × 3 = 12 cups.

questions.stem: Are the ratios 6:9 and 2:3 equivalent?
questions.explanation: Divide 6:9 by 3 to get 2:3. Since both ratios simplify to 2:3, they are equivalent.

questions.stem: If 3 pounds of apples cost $6, how much do 7 pounds cost?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: $6 ÷ 3 = $2 per pound. For 7 pounds: $2 × 7 = $14.

questions.stem: Solve the proportion: 2/5 = x/20. What is x?
questions.explanation: Scale factor: 20 ÷ 5 = 4. Multiply: 2 × 4 = 8. So x = 8.

questions.stem: A chef uses the proportion 3/7 = x/28 to scale a recipe. What is x?
questions.explanation: Scale factor: 28 ÷ 7 = 4. Multiply: 3 × 4 = 12. So x = 12.

questions.stem: Chef Reyes's pasta dough uses 2 eggs for every 3 cups of flour. For a banquet, the kitchen mixes 9 cups of flour. How many eggs are needed to keep the same ratio?
questions.explanation: Scale factor: 9 cups divided by 3 cups = 3. Multiply the eggs by the same factor: 2 x 3 = 6 eggs.

questions.stem: A marinara recipe uses 4 cups of tomatoes for every 6 servings. The chef needs 18 servings. How many cups of tomatoes should she use?
questions.explanation: Scale factor: 18 servings divided by 6 servings = 3. Multiply the tomatoes by 3: 4 x 3 = 12 cups.

questions.stem: During a cooking-team relay, a chef plates 3 finished dishes for every 5 minutes she works. At the same rate, how many dishes will she plate in 20 minutes?
questions.explanation: Scale factor: 20 minutes divided by 5 minutes = 4. Multiply the dishes by 4: 3 x 4 = 12 dishes.

questions.stem: A bakery makes 24 cookies in 3 batches. What is the unit rate of cookies per batch?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: 24 cookies ÷ 3 batches = 8 cookies per batch.

questions.stem: Apples cost $5 for 4 pounds. What is the cost per pound?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: $5 ÷ 4 pounds = $1.25 per pound.

questions.stem: A cyclist rides 36 miles in 3 hours. At the same rate, how far will she ride in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: 36 ÷ 3 = 12 miles per hour. In 5 hours: 12 × 5 = 60 miles.

questions.stem: A printer prints 45 pages in 9 minutes. How many pages does it print per minute?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 pages per minute.

questions.stem: A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. A bus travels 200 miles in 5 hours. Which vehicle is faster?
questions.explanation: Car: 150÷3 = 50 mph. Bus: 200÷5 = 40 mph. The car travels faster at 50 mph vs. 40 mph.

questions.stem: In the kitchen, 3 pizzas feed exactly 12 people. At the same rate, how many pizzas are needed to feed 20 people?
questions.explanation: First find the unit rate: 12 people ÷ 3 pizzas = 4 people per pizza. Then 20 people ÷ 4 people per pizza = 5 pizzas.

questions.stem: A line cook chops 8 carrots in 2 minutes. Working at the same steady rate, how many carrots can the cook chop in 7 minutes?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: 8 carrots ÷ 2 minutes = 4 carrots per minute. In 7 minutes: 4 × 7 = 28 carrots.

questions.stem: Level 2 Extension — Mixed review: A recipe uses 18 ounces of flour to make 3 loaves of bread. How many ounces of flour are needed to make 7 loaves at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: 18 ounces ÷ 3 loaves = 6 ounces per loaf. For 7 loaves: 6 × 7 = 42 ounces. The equivalent ratio 18/3 = 42/7 confirms it.

questions.stem: A booth charges $4.50 for 9 games. What is the unit rate?
A car travels 180 miles using 6 gallons of gas. What is the unit rate in miles per gallon?
questions.explanation: 180 miles ÷ 6 gallons = 30 miles per gallon.

questions.stem: A pack of 8 markers costs $6.00. What is the cost per marker?
Which is a unit rate?
questions.explanation: A unit rate has 1 in the second quantity. '12 miles per 1 hour' is the only choice where the second quantity is 1.

questions.stem: Which token pack from the table above is the best deal?
questions.explanation: Pack B has a unit rate of $0.20 per token, which is the lowest cost per token.

questions.stem: Runner A completes 4 laps in 12 minutes. Runner B completes 5 laps in 14 minutes. Who runs more laps per minute?
questions.explanation: Runner A: 4÷12 ≈ 0.33 laps/min. Runner B: 5÷14 ≈ 0.36 laps/min. Runner B runs slightly more laps per minute.

questions.stem: The Star Blaster cabinet scored 90 points in 3 games. What is the unit rate in points per game?
questions.explanation: Divide points by games: 90 ÷ 3 = 30 points per game.

questions.stem: Two cabinets give points over time. Nova scored 78 points in 6 minutes. Pulse scored 75 points in 5 minutes. Which cabinet has the faster scoring rate (more points per minute)?
choices: They score at the same rate
questions.explanation: Nova: 78 ÷ 6 = 13 points per minute. Pulse: 75 ÷ 5 = 15 points per minute. 15 > 13, so Pulse is faster.

questions.stem: Two claw machines cost coins per play. Machine A charges 150 coins for 5 plays. Machine B charges 168 coins for 8 plays. Which machine is the better value (fewer coins per play)?
choices: Machine B, at 21 coins per play
Machine A, at 30 coins per play
Machine A, because it costs fewer coins total
questions.explanation: Machine A: 150 ÷ 5 = 30 coins per play. Machine B: 168 ÷ 8 = 21 coins per play. 21 < 30, so Machine B is the better value.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Unit Rate"?
questions.explanation: $2 per 1 pound: It gives the amount for exactly one unit.

questions.stem: A booth charges $4.50 for 9 games. What is the unit rate?
A car travels 180 miles using 6 gallons of gas. What is the unit rate in miles per gallon?
questions.explanation: 180 miles ÷ 6 gallons = 30 miles per gallon.

questions.stem: A pack of 8 markers costs $6.00. What is the cost per marker?
Which is a unit rate?
questions.explanation: A unit rate has 1 in the second quantity. '12 miles per 1 hour' is the only choice where the second quantity is 1.

questions.stem: Which token pack from the table above is the best deal?
questions.explanation: Pack B has a unit rate of $0.20 per token, which is the lowest cost per token.

questions.stem: Runner A completes 4 laps in 12 minutes. Runner B completes 5 laps in 14 minutes. Who runs more laps per minute?
questions.explanation: Runner A: 4÷12 ≈ 0.33 laps/min. Runner B: 5÷14 ≈ 0.36 laps/min. Runner B runs slightly more laps per minute.

questions.stem: Lock 1 — Star Blaster Station: The high-score machine flashes '120 points in 4 minutes'. What is the unit rate in points per minute?
questions.explanation: Divide points by minutes: 120 ÷ 4 = 30 points per minute.

questions.stem: Lock 2 — Speed Door: Two racing games unlock the door. Pixel Racer scores 250 points in 5 minutes. Turbo Drift scores 180 points in 4 minutes. Which game earns points at the faster rate?
choices: They earn points at the same rate
questions.explanation: Pixel Racer: 250 ÷ 5 = 50 points per minute. Turbo Drift: 180 ÷ 4 = 45 points per minute. 50 > 45, so Pixel Racer is faster.

questions.stem: Lock 3 — Claw Machine Vault: Three coin deals glow on the screen. Which deal is the best value (lowest cost per play)?
questions.explanation: $5.00 ÷ 10 = $0.50 per play; $6.00 ÷ 8 = $0.75 per play; $9.00 ÷ 12 = $0.75 per play; $7.00 ÷ 10 = $0.70 per play. The lowest unit rate, $0.50 per play, is the best value.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Unit Rate"?
questions.explanation: $2 per 1 pound: It gives the amount for exactly one unit.

questions.stem: Convert 3/5 to a percent.
Convert 7/20 to a percent.
Which decimal is equivalent to 45%?
questions.explanation: To convert a percent to a decimal, divide by 100: 45 ÷ 100 = 0.45.

questions.stem: What fraction is equal to 0.75?
questions.explanation: 0.75 = 75/100. Simplify by dividing both by 25: 75÷25 = 3 and 100÷25 = 4. So 0.75 = 3/4.

questions.stem: A game shows your score as 7/8 complete. What percent is that?
Your arcade scoreboard reads 0.25 of the level cleared. What percent and fraction match this score?
questions.explanation: Move the decimal two places: 0.25 = 25%. As a fraction, 0.25 = 25/100 = 1/4.

questions.stem: A player powered up 3/5 of the energy bar. Which decimal and percent name the same amount?
questions.explanation: Divide 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6, then multiply by 100: 0.6 = 60%. So 3/5 = 0.6 = 60%.

questions.stem: Which statement about "Equivalent" is true?
questions.explanation: Correct: 1/2, 0.5, and 50% are equivalent.

questions.lessonTitle: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
questions.stem: Which of the following is greater than 100%?
questions.explanation: 1.25 = 125%, which is greater than 100%. The other values are all less than 1 (less than 100%).

questions.lessonTitle: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
questions.stem: What is 200% written as a decimal?
questions.explanation: 200% ÷ 100 = 2.0. Percents greater than 100% become decimals greater than 1.

questions.lessonTitle: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
questions.stem: What is 0.5% written as a decimal?
questions.explanation: 0.5% ÷ 100 = 0.005. Move the decimal two places to the left.

questions.lessonTitle: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
questions.stem: Which percent is less than 1%?
questions.explanation: 0.75% is less than 1%. All the other choices are greater than 1%.

questions.lessonTitle: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
questions.stem: A player scored 0.4% of the bonus points. Which decimal represents this percent?
questions.explanation: 0.4% = 0.4 ÷ 100 = 0.004. Move the decimal point two places to the left.

questions.lessonTitle: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
questions.stem: A power-up boosts your damage to 150% of normal. Written as a decimal and a fraction, 150% equals:
questions.explanation: 150% = 150 ÷ 100 = 1.5, and 150/100 simplifies to 3/2. It is more than one whole, so the decimal is greater than 1.

questions.lessonTitle: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
questions.stem: A rare game item has a 0.5% drop chance. What is 0.5% written as a decimal?
questions.explanation: 0.5% = 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005. Because it is less than 1%, the decimal must be less than 0.01.

questions.lessonTitle: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
questions.stem: Could this really happen? Your phone shows it is charged to 0.5% — about how much of a 4,000 mAh battery is that?
choices: About 20 mAh — a tiny sliver, almost empty
questions.explanation: 0.5% = 0.005, and 0.005 × 4,000 = 20 mAh. A percent less than 1% is a tiny part, so the phone is nearly dead.

questions.lessonTitle: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Greater than 100%"?
questions.explanation: 150%: 150% is more than one whole (100%).

questions.lessonTitle: Percents Greater Than 100% and Less Than 1%
questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Less than 1%"?
questions.explanation: 0.5%: 0.5% is smaller than 1%.

questions.lessonTitle: Find the Percent of a Number
questions.stem: What is 20% of 150?

questions.lessonTitle: Find the Percent of a Number
questions.stem: What is 50% of 84?
questions.explanation: 50% = 0.50. Multiply: 0.50 × 84 = 42. (Or simply divide by 2: 84 ÷ 2 = 42.)

questions.lessonTitle: Find the Percent of a Number
questions.stem: What is 10% of 320?
questions.explanation: 10% = 0.10. Multiply: 0.10 × 320 = 32. (Or move the decimal one place left.)

questions.lessonTitle: Find the Percent of a Number
questions.stem: What percent of 50 is 15?

questions.lessonTitle: Find the Percent of a Number
questions.stem: An arcade prize costs 240 tickets. If you have a coupon for 15% off, how many tickets do you save?
questions.explanation: 15% of 240 = 0.15 × 240 = 36 tickets saved.

questions.lessonTitle: Find the Percent of a Number
questions.stem: A student scored 72 out of 90 on a test. What percent did they score?

questions.lessonTitle: Find the Percent of a Number
questions.stem: The claw machine prize is 80 tickets and today it is 25% off. How many tickets do you save?
questions.explanation: 25% = 0.25. Multiply: 0.25 × 80 = 20 tickets saved.

questions.lessonTitle: Find the Percent of a Number
questions.stem: Your bowling score was 60 points. The bonus round adds 15% more points. How many bonus points is that?
questions.explanation: 15% = 0.15. Multiply: 0.15 × 60 = 9 bonus points.

questions.lessonTitle: Find the Percent of a Number
questions.stem: A snack at the arcade costs $40. The sales tax is 5%. How many dollars is the tax?
A prize costs 120 tickets and is 25% off. What is the sale price?
A meal costs $20. You leave a 15% tip. How much is the tip?
A shirt costs $40 and the sales tax is 5%. What is the total cost including tax?
A game originally costs 200 tickets. It is marked up 10%. What is the new price?
questions.explanation: Markup: 0.10 × 200 = 20. New price: 200 + 20 = 220 tickets.

questions.stem: A store marks up a $30 item by 40%, then a customer gets 10% off. What is the final price?
A restaurant bill is $35. You want to leave a 20% tip. What is the total amount you pay?
Store 1 — Sneaker Spot: A pair of sneakers is $60 with 20% off. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Discount: 0.20 x 60 = 12. Sale price: 60 - 12 = $48.

questions.stem: Store 2 — Tech Stop: A $25 phone case has 8% sales tax added. What is the total cost?
Store 3 — Food Court: Your lunch bill is $40. You leave a 15% tip. How much is the tip?
How many inches are in 7 feet?
questions.explanation: 7 × 12 = 84 inches.

questions.stem: How many feet are in 3 yards?
questions.explanation: 1 yard = 3 feet. 3 × 3 = 9 feet.

questions.stem: How many ounces are in 4 pounds?
questions.explanation: 1 pound = 16 ounces. 4 × 16 = 64 ounces.

questions.stem: Convert 24 inches to feet.
A shelf is 30 inches long. How many feet and inches is that?
questions.explanation: 30 ÷ 12 = 2 remainder 6. So 30 inches = 2 feet 6 inches.

questions.stem: Leg 1: The joystick rod is 3 feet long, but the parts catalog lists it in inches. How many inches is that? (1 ft = 12 in)
questions.explanation: Inches are smaller than feet, so multiply: 3 × 12 = 36 inches.

questions.stem: Leg 2: A power cable on the cabinet plan measures 2.5 kilometers across the whole arcade network. How many meters is that? (1 km = 1,000 m)
questions.explanation: Meters are smaller than kilometers, so multiply: 2.5 × 1,000 = 2,500 meters.

questions.stem: Leg 3: The coin box weighs 5 pounds, but the shipping label needs the weight in ounces. How many ounces is that? (1 lb = 16 oz)
questions.explanation: Ounces are smaller than pounds, so multiply: 5 × 16 = 80 ounces.

questions.stem: Final Leg: The finished cabinet ships in a crate holding 8 quarts of packing gel, but the supplier sells gel by the gallon. How many gallons is that? (4 qt = 1 gal)
questions.explanation: Gallons are bigger than quarts, so divide: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 gallons.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Customary units"?
questions.explanation: foot: A foot is a customary unit of length.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Metric units"?
questions.explanation: gram: A gram is a metric unit of mass.

questions.stem: Which is the better buy: 6 bouncy balls for $4.50 or 10 bouncy balls for $8.00?
choices: They cost the same per ball

questions.stem: A faucet drips 15 ounces of water in 5 minutes. What is the unit rate?
questions.explanation: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 ounces per minute.

questions.stem: A printer prints 42 pages in 6 minutes. How many pages does it print in 15 minutes at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 pages per minute. In 15 minutes: 7 × 15 = 105 pages.

questions.stem: Store A sells 5 notebooks for $8. Store B sells 3 notebooks for $5.25. Which has the lower price per notebook?
questions.explanation: Store A: $8 ÷ 5 = $1.60. Store B: $5.25 ÷ 3 = $1.75. $1.60 < $1.75, so Store A is cheaper per notebook.

questions.stem: A machine dispenses 24 tokens in 3 minutes. At this rate, how many tokens does it dispense in 10 minutes?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 tokens per minute. In 10 minutes: 8 × 10 = 80 tokens.

questions.stem: A factory produces 360 widgets in 8 hours. At the same rate, how many widgets are produced in a 12-hour shift?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 widgets per hour. In 12 hours: 45 × 12 = 540 widgets.

questions.stem: The snack bar compares two popcorn deals: 12 oz for $3.00 or 20 oz for $4.00. Which is the better buy?
choices: They cost the same per ounce

questions.stem: The delivery van brings arcade supplies 150 miles in 3 hours. What is the unit rate in miles per hour?
questions.explanation: 150 ÷ 3 = 50 miles per hour.

questions.stem: The ticket counter sells redemption tickets two ways: 8 tickets for $2.00 or 15 tickets for $3.00. Which costs less per ticket?
choices: They cost the same per ticket

questions.stem: What is the area of a parallelogram with base 10 cm and height 7 cm?
questions.explanation: A = b × h = 10 × 7 = 70 square centimeters.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has an area of 54 sq ft and a base of 9 ft. What is the height?
What is the area of a parallelogram with base 9 cm and height 5 cm?
questions.explanation: A = b × h = 9 × 5 = 45 square centimeters.

questions.stem: Which measurement is the height of a parallelogram?
choices: The perpendicular distance between the base and the opposite side
The length of the slanted side
questions.explanation: The height is always the perpendicular (straight up-and-down) distance between the base and the opposite side, not the slanted side.

questions.stem: In the design lab you cut a triangle off the slanted left end of a parallelogram blueprint and slide it to the right end. What shape do you make, and why does it prove A = base x height?
choices: A rectangle with the same base and height, so its area equals base x height
A bigger parallelogram, so the area gets larger
A triangle, so the area is cut in half
A square, so all four sides must be equal
questions.explanation: Sliding the cut triangle turns the parallelogram into a rectangle that keeps the same base and height. A rectangle's area is base x height, so the parallelogram's area is base x height too.

questions.stem: A blueprint parallelogram has a base of 8 ft, a height of 5 ft, and a slanted side of 7 ft. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area = base x height = 8 x 5 = 40 sq ft. The 7 ft slanted side is not used; only the perpendicular height belongs in the formula.

questions.stem: Two blueprints share a base of 10 ft. Blueprint M has height 6 ft; Blueprint N is more tilted with the same height of 6 ft but a longer slanted side of 9 ft. How do their areas compare?
choices: Equal: both are 10 x 6 = 60 sq ft because area depends on base and height, not the slant
Blueprint N is larger because its slanted side is 9 ft
Blueprint M is larger because it is less tilted
You cannot compare them without the slanted side of M
questions.explanation: Area = base x height. Both have base 10 ft and height 6 ft, so both areas are 10 x 6 = 60 sq ft. Tilting the shape changes the slanted side but not the perpendicular height, so the area stays the same.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Parallelogram"?
choices: A slanted four-sided shape with both pairs of sides parallel
questions.explanation: A slanted four-sided shape with both pairs of sides parallel: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.

questions.stem: What is the area of a trapezoid with bases 6 cm and 10 cm, and height 4 cm?
A trapezoid has an area of 45 sq ft, bases of 7 ft and 11 ft. What is the height?
What is the first step when finding the area of a trapezoid?
choices: Subtract the shorter base from the longer base
questions.explanation: The formula is A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. The first step is to add the two parallel bases.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has bases of 5 in and 9 in, and a height of 6 in. What is its area?
Blueprint 1: A trapezoidal lobby window has bases of 6 ft and 10 ft and a height of 4 ft. What is its area for the glass order?
Blueprint 2: A trapezoidal skylight has bases of 9 ft and 7 ft and a height of 6 ft. What is its area?

Level 2 Extension: Two copies of a trapezoidal window (bases 5 ft and 11 ft) are flipped and joined to make a parallelogram with height 6 ft. The parallelogram's base is 5 + 11 = 16 ft, so its area is 96 sq ft. What is the area of ONE trapezoid window?
questions.explanation: One trapezoid is half the parallelogram: 96 ÷ 2 = 48 sq ft. This matches A = ½ × (5 + 11) × 6 = ½ × 16 × 6 = 48 sq ft — the ½ comes from the trapezoid being half of the parallelogram.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Trapezoid"?
choices: A four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides
questions.explanation: A four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides: It has exactly one pair of parallel sides.

questions.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 square centimeters.

questions.stem: A triangle has an area of 24 sq ft and a base of 8 ft. What is the height?
Why do we divide by 2 when finding the area of a triangle?
choices: A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height
The base is always twice the height
We always divide area formulas by 2
questions.explanation: A triangle with base b and height h fits inside a rectangle with the same base and height. The triangle covers exactly half the rectangle, so A = ½ × b × h.

questions.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 14 ft and height 6 ft?
A triangular window in the firm's lobby has a base of 10 ft and a height of 6 ft. What is its area?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = ½ × 60 = 30 sq ft. The triangle is half of the 10 × 6 = 60 rectangle it fits inside.

questions.stem: A triangular roof panel on the blueprint has a base of 7 ft and a height of 4 ft. What is its area?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 7 × 4 = ½ × 28 = 14 sq ft. Multiply base × height first (28), then take half (14).

questions.stem: On the blueprint, a triangular garden bed has a base of 11 ft and a height of 6 ft. What is its area?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 11 × 6 = ½ × 66 = 33 sq ft.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Perpendicular"?
choices: Two lines meeting at a 90° angle
questions.explanation: Two lines meeting at a 90° angle: Perpendicular lines form a right angle.

questions.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 square centimeters.

questions.stem: A triangle has an area of 24 sq ft and a base of 8 ft. What is the height?
What is the area of a triangle with base 14 ft and height 6 ft?
A triangular window pane has a base of 9 in and a height of 4 in. What is its area?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × 9 × 4 = ½ × 36 = 18 square inches.

questions.stem: Which formula gives the area of a triangle with base b and height h?
questions.explanation: A triangle covers exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height, so A = ½ × b × h.

questions.stem: A triangular sail has an area of 30 sq m and a height of 12 m. What is its base?
A composite logo is made of a rectangle (8 cm by 6 cm) with a triangle on top. The triangle has a base of 8 cm and a height of 5 cm. What is the total area of the logo?
questions.explanation: Rectangle: 8 × 6 = 48 sq cm. Triangle: ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 sq cm. Total: 48 + 20 = 68 sq cm.

questions.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 16 m and height 5 m?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × 16 × 5 = ½ × 80 = 40 square meters.

questions.stem: A triangle has an area of 36 sq cm and a height of 9 cm. What is its base?
Two triangles have the same area. One has a base of 12 ft and a height of 6 ft. The other has a base of 9 ft. What is the height of the second triangle?
questions.explanation: First area = ½ × 12 × 6 = 36 sq ft. Then 36 = ½ × 9 × h → 36 = 4.5h → h = 8 ft.

questions.stem: You design a triangular roof gable for a client's cabin. The base measures 8 ft and the height measures 5 ft. What is the area of the gable?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 8 × 5 = ½ × 40 = 20 square feet.

questions.stem: A triangular flag has a base of 12 in along the pole. Its two slanted sides measure 10 in, but a dashed line shows the perpendicular height is 7 in. What is the area of the flag?
questions.explanation: Use the perpendicular height (7 in), not a slanted side. A = ½ × 12 × 7 = ½ × 84 = 42 square inches.

questions.stem: Your studio designs a triangular road sign with a base of 6 ft and a height of 9 ft. What is its area?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × 6 × 9 = ½ × 54 = 27 square feet.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Perpendicular"?
choices: Two lines meeting at a 90° angle
questions.explanation: Two lines meeting at a 90° angle: Perpendicular lines form a right angle.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon is divided into 6 equal triangles from the center. Each triangle has a base of 6 ft and a height of 5.2 ft. What is the area of one triangle?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 square feet.

questions.stem: Using the triangle from the previous question, what is the total area of the hexagonal skylight?
questions.explanation: Total area = 6 triangles × 15.6 sq ft = 93.6 square feet.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon is split into 6 triangles, each with base 4 cm and height 3.5 cm. What is the total area?
questions.explanation: Each triangle: ½ × 4 × 3.5 = 7 sq cm. Total: 6 × 7 = 42 sq cm.

questions.stem: How many triangles can you make from the center of a regular pentagon?
questions.explanation: A regular pentagon has 5 sides, so drawing lines from the center to each vertex creates 5 equal triangles.

questions.stem: A regular hexagonal floor tile splits from its center into 6 congruent triangles, each with an area of 12 cm². What is the total area of the tile?
questions.explanation: A hexagon has 6 sides, so it splits into 6 equal triangles. Total = 6 × 12 = 72 cm².

questions.stem: A regular pentagonal tile splits into 5 congruent triangles. Each triangle has a base of 4 in and a height of 6 in. What is the total area of the tile?
questions.explanation: One triangle = ½ × 4 × 6 = 12 in². A pentagon has 5 triangles, so total = 5 × 12 = 60 in².

questions.stem: A regular octagonal tile is split from its center into congruent triangles. Each triangle has a base of 6 ft and a height of 5 ft. First decide how many triangles an octagon has, then find the total area.
questions.explanation: An octagon has 8 sides, so it splits into 8 triangles. One triangle = ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 sq ft. Total = 8 × 15 = 120 sq ft.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Regular Polygon"?
choices: A rectangle that is not a square
questions.explanation: A square: All sides and all angles are equal.

questions.stem: An L-shaped room is made of two rectangles: 10 ft × 6 ft and 4 ft × 3 ft. What is the total area?
questions.explanation: Area 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Area 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.

questions.stem: A rectangular patio is 15 ft × 10 ft with a 5 ft × 4 ft rectangular flower bed cut out. What is the remaining area?
questions.explanation: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Cutout = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Remaining = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.

questions.stem: Find the area of an L-shape made of a 5×3 rectangle and a 2×4 rectangle.
When should you subtract areas instead of adding them to find the area of a composite figure?
choices: When a piece is cut out or removed from a larger shape
When one shape is larger than the other
questions.explanation: Subtract when a piece is removed from a larger shape (like a window cut from a wall). Add when two shapes are joined together (like an L-shape).

questions.stem: Plan 1 — Office wing: the floor plan is a 7 ft by 5 ft rectangle with a triangular reading nook (base 7 ft, height 4 ft) joined on top. Decompose it and ADD the areas. What is the total floor area?
questions.explanation: Rectangle = 7 x 5 = 35 sq ft. Triangle = 1/2 x 7 x 4 = 14 sq ft. The pieces are joined, so add: 35 + 14 = 49 sq ft.

questions.stem: Plan 2 — L-shaped lobby: decompose the L into two rectangles, one 9 ft by 6 ft and one 7 ft by 3 ft, then ADD. What is the total floor area?
questions.explanation: First rectangle = 9 x 6 = 54 sq ft. Second rectangle = 7 x 3 = 21 sq ft. Joined L-shape, so add: 54 + 21 = 75 sq ft.

questions.stem: Plan 4 — Design studio: the floor is a 16 ft by 12 ft rectangle, but a 5 ft by 4 ft storage closet is cut out of one corner. Find the usable floor area.
questions.explanation: Large rectangle = 16 x 12 = 192 sq ft. Cutout closet = 5 x 4 = 20 sq ft. A piece is removed, so subtract: 192 - 20 = 172 sq ft.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Composite Figure"?
choices: An L-shaped room made of two rectangles
questions.explanation: An L-shaped room made of two rectangles: It is built from two basic shapes.

questions.stem: What is the value of 4³?
What is the value of 6²?
Which expression shows 5³ as repeated multiplication?
questions.explanation: 5³ means use 5 as a factor 3 times: 5 × 5 × 5. The exponent tells how many times to multiply, not what to multiply by.

questions.stem: Evaluate: 3 × (4 + 2)²
The drum loop plays 3⁴ beats. What is the value of 3⁴?
questions.explanation: 3⁴ means use 3 as a factor 4 times: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. It is NOT 3 × 4 = 12.

questions.stem: A synth pattern repeats 7 × 7 × 7. How do you write that as a power?
questions.explanation: The base 7 is used as a factor 3 times, so the power is 7³. 7³ = 7 × 7 × 7 = 343.

questions.stem: The bass line doubles for 2⁶ counts. What is the value of 2⁶?
questions.explanation: 2⁶ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 64. The exponent 6 counts how many times 2 is a factor.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Exponent"?
questions.explanation: The 4 in 3⁴: It shows 3 is multiplied 4 times.

questions.stem: What is the value of 4³?
What is the value of 6²?
Which expression shows 5³ as repeated multiplication?
questions.explanation: 5³ means use 5 as a factor 3 times: 5 × 5 × 5. The exponent tells how many times to multiply, not what to multiply by.

questions.stem: Evaluate: 3 × (4 + 2)²
Track 1 is locked. The keypad shows 2³. What value unlocks it?
questions.explanation: 2³ means 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, so 8 unlocks Track 1.

questions.stem: Track 2 needs the value of 5². Which number opens the door?
questions.explanation: 5² means 5 × 5 = 25, so 25 unlocks Track 2.

questions.stem: The vault display reads 10⁴. In the power 10⁴, which number is the base?
questions.explanation: The base is the number being multiplied repeatedly. In 10⁴ the base is 10 and the exponent is 4, so 10⁴ = 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 10000.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Exponent"?
questions.explanation: The 4 in 3⁴: It shows 3 is multiplied 4 times.

questions.stem: Evaluate 3x + 7 when x = 4.
Evaluate 20 − 2n when n = 6.
Which expression means '5 less than twice a number n'?
questions.explanation: Twice n is 2n. Five less than that is 2n − 5.

questions.stem: Evaluate 4m + 1 when m = 5.
Track 1 — The beat formula is 3x + 5, where x is the number of bass drops. Evaluate 3x + 5 when x = 4.
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 4: 3(4) + 5. Multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12. Then add: 12 + 5 = 17.

questions.stem: Track 2 — The volume mix is 2(n + 3), where n is the number of monitors. Evaluate 2(n + 3) when n = 5.
questions.explanation: Substitute n = 5: 2(5 + 3). Do the parentheses first: 5 + 3 = 8. Then multiply: 2 × 8 = 16.

questions.stem: Track 3 — The speaker power is x², where x is the gain setting. Evaluate x² when x = 6.
questions.explanation: x² means x times itself. Substitute x = 6: 6² = 6 × 6 = 36.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Expression"?
questions.explanation: 3x + 5: It has terms and operations but no equal sign.

questions.stem: Which expression represents 'the product of 6 and a number n'?
questions.explanation: 'Product' means multiplication, so the product of 6 and n is 6n.

questions.stem: Which expression represents '9 less than a number y'?
questions.explanation: 'Less than' means subtract from the number, so it's y − 9.

questions.stem: Which expression represents 'the sum of a number m and 15'?
questions.explanation: 'Sum' means addition, so the sum of m and 15 is m + 15.

questions.stem: Which key word tells you to multiply?
questions.explanation: 'Product' means multiplication. 'Sum' means addition, 'difference' means subtraction, and 'quotient' means division.

questions.stem: Line 1: A lyric says '7 more than a number of beats n.' Which expression matches?
questions.explanation: 'More than' means addition, so '7 more than n' is n + 7.

questions.stem: Line 2: The chorus says '5 less than a number of tracks x.' Which expression matches?
questions.explanation: 'Less than' subtracts from the number: start with x and take away 5, so x − 5.

questions.stem: Line 3: A verse says 'twice a number of speakers' (use s). Which expression matches?
questions.explanation: 'Twice' means two times the number, so twice s is 2s.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Coefficient"?
questions.explanation: The 7 in 7n: It is the number multiplied by the variable n.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Constant"?
questions.explanation: The 5 in 3x + 5: It is a number with no variable.

questions.stem: Which property is shown? 5 + 13 = 13 + 5
questions.explanation: The order of the addends changed, so this is the Commutative Property of Addition.

questions.stem: Which property is shown? (6 × 3) × 2 = 6 × (3 × 2)
questions.explanation: The grouping (parentheses) changed but the order stayed the same, so this is the Associative Property of Multiplication.

questions.stem: Which property is shown? 47 + 0 = 47
questions.explanation: Adding 0 does not change the value, so this is the Identity Property of Addition.

questions.stem: Which property lets you rearrange 8 × 5 to 5 × 8?
questions.explanation: Changing the order of factors is the Commutative Property of Multiplication.

questions.stem: Track 2 on the playlist plays 5(7 + 2) = 5 × 7 + 5 × 2. Which property is this?
questions.explanation: Multiplying 5 across both numbers inside the parentheses (5 × 7 and 5 × 2) shows the Distributive Property.

questions.stem: Track 3 plays (7 + 3) + 5 = 7 + (3 + 5). Only the parentheses moved. Which property is this?
questions.explanation: The grouping (parentheses) changed but the order of the numbers stayed the same, so this is the Associative Property.

questions.stem: Track 4 plays 1 × y = y. Which property is this?
questions.explanation: Multiplying by 1 keeps the same value, so this is the Identity Property of Multiplication.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Commutative Property"?
questions.explanation: 4 + 7 = 7 + 4: Changing the order keeps the same sum.

questions.stem: Expand 6(n + 3) using the distributive property.
Expand 4(5 − 2) using the distributive property.
Expand 3(x + 4) using the distributive property.
When using the distributive property with a(b + c), you must multiply 'a' by:
questions.explanation: The distributive property says a(b + c) = ab + ac. You multiply the outside factor by EACH term inside the parentheses.

questions.stem: Light Cue 1: Expand 3(x + 4) for the stage-light controller.
questions.explanation: Distribute the 3 to each term: 3 × x + 3 × 4 = 3x + 12.

questions.stem: Light Cue 2: Expand 5(2 + n) to set two spotlight banks.
questions.explanation: Distribute the 5 to each term: 5 × 2 + 5 × n = 10 + 5n.

questions.stem: Light Cue 3: Expand 4(a + 2) for the back-row beam.
questions.explanation: Distribute the 4 to each term: 4 × a + 4 × 2 = 4a + 8.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Distributive Property"?
questions.explanation: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12: The 3 is multiplied by each term inside.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 4x + 3x?
questions.explanation: 4x + 3x = 7x. Combine the coefficients: 4 + 3 = 7.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 2(m + 5)?
questions.explanation: 2(m + 5) = 2m + 10 using the distributive property.

questions.stem: Which property is shown: 3(x + 7) = 3x + 21?
questions.explanation: Multiplying 3 by each term inside the parentheses is the distributive property.

questions.stem: Simplify: 5n + 2n
questions.explanation: 5n + 2n = 7n. Add the coefficients: 5 + 2 = 7. The variable stays as n.

questions.stem: Producer A wrote 2(x + 3) for a beat's cost. Which expression is equivalent?
questions.explanation: Distribute the 2 to each term inside: 2 · x + 2 · 3 = 2x + 6. Check x = 5: 2(5 + 3) = 16 and 2(5) + 6 = 16.

questions.stem: A track stacks 3x and then one more x. Which expression is equivalent to 3x + x?
questions.explanation: 3x + x is 3 groups of x plus 1 more group of x = 4x. Add the coefficients: 3 + 1 = 4. Check x = 3: 3(3) + 3 = 12 and 4(3) = 12.

questions.stem: Producer B flipped a formula to 5 + 2x. Which expression is equivalent?
questions.explanation: Order of addition does not change the value (commutative property): 5 + 2x = 2x + 5. Check x = 10: 5 + 2(10) = 25 and 2(10) + 5 = 25.

questions.stem: Which statement about "Equivalent" is true?
questions.explanation: Correct: 2x + 3x and 5x are equivalent expressions.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Like Terms"?

questions.stem: Simplify 7x + 3x.

questions.stem: Simplify 9n + 4 + 2n.
questions.explanation: 9n + 2n = 11n. The constant 4 has no like term, so it stays. Result: 11n + 4.

questions.stem: Which pair are like terms?
questions.explanation: 6x and 2x are like terms because they both have the same variable (x) raised to the same power (1).

questions.stem: Simplify 5a + 3 + 2a.
questions.explanation: 5a + 2a = 7a. The constant 3 stays. Result: 7a + 3.

questions.stem: The board shows 3x + 5x on one channel. Simplify it.
questions.explanation: 3x and 5x are like terms, so add the coefficients: 3 + 5 = 8. The variable x stays, giving 8x.

questions.stem: Simplify the track: 4a + 2 + a.
questions.explanation: 4a + a = 5a (remember a means 1a). The 2 has no like term, so it stays. Result: 5a + 2.

questions.stem: Clean up this channel: 7y − 3y.
questions.explanation: Subtract the coefficients of the like terms: 7 − 3 = 4. Keep the variable y, giving 4y.

questions.stem: Simplify the mix: 6m + 4 + 3m.
questions.explanation: 6m + 3m = 9m. The constant 4 has no like term, so it stays. Result: 9m + 4.

questions.stem: Which one is an example of "Like Terms"?
